section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Emergency vehicles using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights:
options: a:Have the right-of-way and drivers must yield to them.,b:May follow each other and you should proceed only when sure the way is clear.,c:May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or lights; obey instructions and ensure the path is clear before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What shape/color represents the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:Reflective orange triangle (commonly shown on a yellow/orange background),b:Rectangular red sign,c:Circular green sign,d:Diamond-shaped yellow sign
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange (sometimes bordered) triangle indicating a vehicle likely traveling 25 mph or less.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which are ways alcoholic beverages can affect you?
options: a:They slow reaction time, impair thinking, and give a false sense of confidence.,b:They always improve alertness.,c:They only cause sleepiness but not coordination problems.,d:They only affect people who are under 21.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, impairs judgment and thinking, and can produce false confidence and poor coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.,b:All crossings have flashing signals and gates.,c:You never need to stop if no train is visible.
note: Driving around lowered gates is unlawful. Not all crossings have gates or signals; always obey signs, flags, and warning devices.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are involved in an accident as a driver, you should:
options: a:Exchange information such as names, addresses, license and insurance details.,b:Refuse to share any details.,c:Leave immediately and call later.,d:Only give your name without other details.
note: Exchange full information with other drivers, including names, addresses, license numbers, vehicle data, and insurance details.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turn signal lights on vehicles manufactured after 1955 must be visible for at least how many feet?
options: a:250 feet,b:300 feet,c:500 feet
note: Required front and rear turn signal lamps must be visible for at least 300 feet in normal daylight conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the centerline shows a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear
note: When the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross to pass if no oncoming traffic is present and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A single broken white line between lanes indicates what?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you encounter a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, then proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping,c:Wait until a green light appears,d:Yield only to pedestrians
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign: stop fully, then go when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When weather changes suddenly, what should you do?
options: a:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,b:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.,c:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
note: If the weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving to match conditions — slow down in rain or fog and be aware of vehicles behind you that may not be slowing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Stop and do not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes.,b:The arrow is decorative only and may be ignored,c:Proceed with caution and yield to pedestrians,d:You may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic
note: A solid red arrow indicates traffic in that lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction until it changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer stops your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.,c:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands visible on the wheel and wait for the officer’s instructions; only retrieve documents when asked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,d:Leave the wheels in neutral
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so if brakes fail the vehicle rolls into the curb rather than into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and only cross when you are sure no train is coming.,b:Turn down the radio to try to hear a train.,c:Only proceed if a flagger clears you to go.
note: Always approach crossings cautiously and do not cross until you have determined no train is coming; obey any flagger if present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
options: a:Blind or visually impaired.,b:Deaf.,c:Part of a traffic study.,d:Directing traffic.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is using a white cane or guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street,b:In the center of the roadway,c:In the right lane of the one-way street,d:Across two lanes
note: When turning left onto a one-way street from a two-way street, complete the turn into the leftmost lane available on the one-way street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather,b:Human error,c:New drivers
note: Most crashes are caused by human error — mistakes like failing to see other vehicles, misjudging distance, or making poor decisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always signal when:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,d:All of the above
note: Use turn signals to indicate your intentions whenever changing lanes, entering traffic, or parking so other road users can respond.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A shared center lane on a two-way road is reserved for:
options: a:Making left turns.,b:Passing slow-moving traffic.,c:Through traffic.
note: Shared center lanes are for left turns (and U-turns where permitted), not for passing or through traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If other drivers are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:React with hand gestures.,b:Distance yourself from the situation and avoid eye contact.,c:Make eye contact to defuse the situation.
note: Mentally and physically distance yourself: avoid eye contact or gestures, slow down or change lanes, and remove yourself safely from the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.,b:Ensure that your tires are properly inflated.,c:Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.,d:All of the above
note: Prevent hydroplaning by keeping tires in good condition and reducing speed in wet conditions; hydroplaning is most likely at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, you should look toward which part of the road?
options: a:The right side of the road.,b:The center of the road.,c:Either side equally.,d:The left shoulder.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded by high beams while maintaining your lane position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Flash your lights to let them know they're wrong.,b:Call the police immediately.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: Avoid escalation by staying calm and getting out of the aggressive driver's path; do not engage or retaliate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign serves to:
options: a:Warn you about conditions on or near the road.,b:Help direct you to cities and towns ahead.,c:Inform you about traffic laws and regulations.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow-and-black signs are warning signs that advise of conditions or hazards ahead on the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which will help someone overcome the influence of alcohol?
options: a:Fresh air,b:Hot coffee,c:Tomato juice and lime,d:Only the passage of time
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, fresh air, or other remedies do not reduce intoxication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above
note: Braking distance is influenced by speed, vehicle maintenance (brakes and tires), and road surface conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see an animal on the road, what is the correct action?
options: a:Pass the animal as closely as possible.,b:No special action is required.,c:Proceed cautiously and pass slowly to avoid startling it.
note: Slow down and pass animals carefully to avoid frightening them and causing unpredictable movement that could cause a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash most commonly indicates:
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That an action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers should yield to others.
note: A red circle with a slash over a black symbol indicates the action shown is prohibited by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left lane and want to move into the right lane, you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for vehicles before changing lanes.,b:Look over your left shoulder only.,c:Signal and immediately move right without checking mirrors.,d:Honk and move over quickly.
note: When changing lanes to the right, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your right shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection with a steady green light, you should:
options: a:Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.,c:Stop if a police officer is nearby.
note: You may go on green but must yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection and be prepared to stop if conditions change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:Either one may proceed at will,c:The vehicle on the right must yield,d:The faster vehicle goes first
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:The bicyclist may swerve unexpectedly or obstacles may force them into traffic.,b:Bicycles always have the right-of-way in every situation.,c:Oncoming traffic cannot see you if you pass a bicycle,d:Bicyclists are required to hug the curb at all times
note: Cyclists may need to swerve to avoid debris or hazards; give them space and pass carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Disregard obvious defects to avoid embarrassment.,b:Assume all vehicles work the same and just start driving.,c:Familiarize yourself with the controls and check for defects before driving.
note: Before driving an unfamiliar car, locate and test signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn; correct any defects first.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: Defensive driving is best described as:
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead very closely.,b:Driving only during daylight hours.,c:Racing to get ahead of aggressive drivers.,d:Identifying dangerous situations early and taking action to avoid collisions.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road, spotting potential hazards early, and adjusting your speed or position to avoid trouble. Instead of reacting at the last second, you leave space, anticipate other drivers’ mistakes, and make calm, safe choices to prevent collisions.

section-name: Signs, Signals & Road Markings
question: Which feature is sometimes used on highways to channel drivers into the correct turning lanes?
options: a:Lane-use arrows and words painted on the pavement,b:Flashing yellow lights,c:Flashing red lights
note: Highways often use lane-use arrows and words painted directly on the pavement to guide drivers into the correct turning or through lanes in advance of an intersection. These pavement markings help drivers choose the proper lane early and reduce last‑second lane changes.

section-name: Signs, Signals & Road Markings
question: What do downward-facing triangular traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:School zones,b:Yield signs,c:Construction zones
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the shape used for yield signs. When you see this sign, slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary to let other vehicles or pedestrians go first.

section-name: Driving in Special Conditions
question: What's the key rule about managing speed when negotiating curves?
options: a:Brake hard in the middle of the curve,b:Slow down before entering the curve, not while at the sharpest point.,c:Maintain posted speed through the entire curve regardless,d:Accelerate before you enter a curve to maintain momentum
note: You should reduce speed before entering a curve, not while you are at the sharpest part. Braking hard in the middle of a curve can cause skidding or loss of control. Enter at a safe speed, then maintain a steady speed and accelerate gently as you exit if conditions allow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multilane highway, you must:
options: a:Signal and ensure the passing lane is clear.,b:Pass only on the right under all circumstances.,c:Assume oncoming traffic will stop.,d:Sound your horn before changing lanes.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, you must check that the lane you will move into is clear of traffic, check your mirrors and blind spot, and signal before changing lanes. Never assume other drivers will slow or stop for you; it is your responsibility to make sure the maneuver can be done safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked ahead by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Do not enter the intersection; wait until you can pass completely through.,b:Edge forward until you can see better,c:Enter the intersection and stop in the middle,d:Honk to signal other drivers to move
note: You should not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it without stopping. Entering when traffic is backed up can leave your vehicle blocking the intersection, which is unsafe, causes gridlock, and is illegal in many jurisdictions.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:
options: a:Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle for the other driver to pass.,b:Speed up to prevent the pass.,c:Move off the road immediately.,d:Flash your headlights and maintain speed.
note: If another driver wants to pass you, help them do it safely. Slightly reduce your speed to create more space in front of you so the passing driver has a larger gap to move back into your lane without cutting too closely in front of you.

section-name: Driving in Special Conditions
question: At night, what is the hardest to see compared to signs and other objects?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Other motorists.,c:Pedestrians.
note: At night, pedestrians are much harder to see than illuminated road signs or vehicles with lights. They may wear dark clothing and are not lit, so you must use your headlights properly, reduce speed, and scan carefully for people near or crossing the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle:
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign.,b:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,c:Where there is a red light.,d:In all of the above situations
note: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop. Failing to stop in any of these situations is illegal and unsafe, so “all of the above” is correct.

section-name: Driving in Special Conditions
question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive faster to get through wet areas quickly.,b:Drive more slowly in wet conditions.,c:Follow closely behind the vehicle ahead.,d:Shift to neutral when water is deep.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. Slowing down in wet conditions helps your tires push water aside and maintain traction, greatly reducing the risk of hydroplaning.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: Faced with an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, you should:
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder.,b:Split the difference.,c:Let the car pass and then pass the bicyclist.
note: When you face an oncoming car on the left and a bicyclist on the right, do not try to squeeze between them. First, let the oncoming car pass. Then, when the lane is clear and it is safe, move over and pass the bicyclist with plenty of space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left goes first,b:Both must wait for a signal,c:The larger vehicle proceeds first,d:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; the vehicle on the left yields.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there is no traffic signal and both drivers arrive together.

section-name: Alcohol, Drugs & Impaired Driving
question: The effect alcohol has on reflexes and judgment is:
options: a:Most pronounced when consuming hard ciders and mixed drinks.,b:Less pronounced when consuming beer instead of wine.,c:Less pronounced when consuming wine instead of beer.,d:Dependent on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream, not the type of beverage.
note: Alcohol’s effect on your reflexes and judgment depends on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream (your BAC), not whether it came from beer, wine, or liquor. A standard serving of each has about the same amount of pure alcohol, so any type can impair you equally if it results in the same BAC.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: If another driver is trying to pass you, you should:
options: a:Brake sharply to discourage them.,b:Pull completely off the road.,c:Speed up to block the pass.,d:Maintain a steady speed or slightly reduce speed so the passing driver can complete the pass safely.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed or slightly reduce your speed so they can pass safely. Do not speed up or brake suddenly. You do not need to check for oncoming traffic—that is the responsibility of the passing driver. Your job is to keep your vehicle’s movement predictable so the pass can be completed safely.

section-name: Signs, Signals & Road Markings
question: What color are regulatory signs usually, and must they be obeyed?
options: a:Blue and optional to follow,b:Green and advisory only,c:Yellow and warn about hazards,d:White background with black markings; they must always be obeyed.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. In the U.S., these are most commonly white with black letters or symbols, and they are legally enforceable, so you must obey them.

section-name: Signs, Signals & Road Markings
question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either side. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you must not use the opposing lane to pass other vehicles.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: What should your first response be to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and stop in the lane,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Turn on your interior light.,d:Reduce your speed.
note: When visibility is reduced, your first response should be to slow down. Reducing speed increases your time to see hazards and react safely. You should also use your headlights and windshield wipers as needed, but immediately lowering your speed is the most important first step to stay safe.
